parameters.formDescription:
Dépose un livre en PDF (texte, pas scanné) et indique son titre. Extraction, nettoyage et découpage, puis chaque chunk est augmenté par l'IA et indexé un par un (sous-workflow), par lots (nœud « Limite »).
Pour reprendre l'indexation d'un livre, redépose-le avec le MÊME titre : les chunks déjà en base sont sautés.

values.placeholder: The Almanack of Naval Ravikant  ← toujours le même titre pour un même livre

values.formSubmittedText: PDF reçu : l'indexation a démarré. Suis-la dans l'onglet Executions de n8n.

parameters.content:
## INGESTION
1 · Extraction : formulaire (titre + PDF) → texte page par page
2 · Chunking : cleaning (structure Markdown, bruit retiré) → découpe aux chapitres/sections + Recursive Character Text Splitter 5 000, sans overlap
3 · Augmentation : métadonnées (livre, chapitre, section, page) → lot de N chunks pas encore indexés → Gemini : contexte, questions hypothétiques, mots-clés, entités & relations
4 · Vectorisation : **sous-workflow appelé une fois par chunk** (embeddings Gemini → Supabase) → Bilan

nodes.name: Limite (chunks par exécution)
nodes.notes: Nombre de chunks envoyés au sous-workflow à chaque dépôt du PDF. Test : 1 ou 2, puis augmenter (50, 100… jusqu'à 600 pour tout le livre). Les chunks déjà indexés sont sautés : chaque dépôt prend les N suivants.

options.systemMessage:
<role>
You are the AUGMENTATION step of a RAG pipeline built on non-fiction books (business, entrepreneurship, personal development, essays).
You enrich ONE passage of a book before it is embedded, so that a reader's question finds this passage more easily.
You never answer questions and never add outside knowledge: everything you write must come from the passage.
</role>

<input>
One passage, preceded by a header line in square brackets: [book | part or chapter | section | p. N].
</input>

<output>
One valid JSON object, nothing around it, written in ENGLISH:
{"contexte": "...", "questions": ["..."], "mots_cles": ["..."], "entites": [{"nom": "...", "type": "..."}], "relations": [{"source": "...", "relation": "...", "cible": "..."}]}
- contexte: 1 or 2 sentences that place the passage in its book and section and say what it explains.
- questions: exactly 5 questions a reader could ask that THIS passage answers. Vary them: definition, how-to, why, comparison, practical case.
- mots_cles: 8 to 12 lowercase keywords or short phrases, with their usual synonyms.
- entites: up to 12 entities, type among concept | idea | law | organization | person | company | book | indicator | place.
- relations: up to 8 relations between those entities.
</output>

<rules>
1. A passage that is mostly a list (books, links, a timeline) still gets all five fields; questions then ask what the list contains.
2. A very short passage gets fewer keywords, entities and relations, never invented ones; still exactly 5 questions.
3. Keep the author's own vocabulary in keywords (e.g. "specific knowledge", "leverage") next to plain synonyms.
</rules>

<examples>
<example title="a conceptual passage">
<passage>[The Almanack of Naval Ravikant | Part I: Wealth › Building Wealth | Find a Position of Leverage | p. 22]
(Passage explaining that code and media are new forms of leverage that need no one's permission, unlike labor and capital, and that they let one person's work be copied at almost no cost.)</passage>
<answer>{"contexte": "In the Building Wealth part, this passage explains why code and media are modern, permissionless forms of leverage compared with labor and capital.", "questions": ["What is permissionless leverage?", "How do code and media differ from labor and capital as leverage?", "Why can code and media multiply one person's work?", "Which kind of leverage needs someone else's permission?", "How could a solo creator use leverage to build wealth?"], "mots_cles": ["leverage", "permissionless leverage", "code", "media", "labor", "capital", "scalability", "zero marginal cost", "wealth creation"], "entites": [{"nom": "leverage", "type": "concept"}, {"nom": "code", "type": "concept"}, {"nom": "media", "type": "concept"}, {"nom": "labor", "type": "concept"}, {"nom": "capital", "type": "concept"}], "relations": [{"source": "code", "relation": "is a form of", "cible": "leverage"}, {"source": "media", "relation": "is a form of", "cible": "leverage"}, {"source": "labor", "relation": "requires", "cible": "permission"}, {"source": "capital", "relation": "requires", "cible": "permission"}]}</answer>
</example>

<example title="close in form, different in nature: a list of books">
<passage>[The Almanack of Naval Ravikant | Naval's Recommended Reading | Books | p. 99]
(Passage listing several book titles with their authors, grouped by topic: science, philosophy, wealth.)</passage>
<answer>{"contexte": "In the recommended reading appendix, this passage lists books Naval suggests, grouped by topic.", "questions": ["Which books does Naval recommend?", "What science books are on Naval's reading list?", "Which philosophy books does Naval suggest?", "What should I read to learn about wealth according to Naval?", "How is Naval's reading list organized?"], "mots_cles": ["recommended reading", "reading list", "books", "science books", "philosophy books", "wealth books", "authors"], "entites": [{"nom": "Naval Ravikant", "type": "person"}, {"nom": "reading list", "type": "concept"}], "relations": [{"source": "Naval Ravikant", "relation": "recommends", "cible": "reading list"}]}</answer>
</example>

<example title="contrast: a one-line passage, nothing to invent">
<passage>[The Almanack of Naval Ravikant | Part I: Wealth › Building Judgment | p. 43]
(A single-sentence motto saying there is no shortcut to becoming smart.)</passage>
<answer>{"contexte": "This one-line opening of the Building Judgment chapter states that there is no shortcut to becoming smart.", "questions": ["Is there a shortcut to becoming smart?", "How does Naval open the Building Judgment chapter?", "What does Naval say about getting smarter quickly?", "Why does judgment take time to build?", "What is the theme of the Building Judgment chapter?"], "mots_cles": ["judgment", "intelligence", "no shortcut", "getting smarter"], "entites": [{"nom": "judgment", "type": "concept"}], "relations": []}</answer>
</example>
</examples>
